title: Reorder shuffled video frames by motion continuity
premise: A fixed-camera clip's frames were saved in a shuffled order; the true capture order must be reconstructed from visual/motion continuity alone, and a naive nearest-neighbor-by-pixel-difference chaining breaks on repeated or near-static frames.
spec: Write /app/reorder.py (Python; cv2, numpy, toml only) that takes a directory of PNG frames named by shuffled index and writes /app/output.toml with field order = [list of the input filenames in reconstructed capture order]. A worked example clip /app/example/ with its known order is provided. All test clips share the example's resolution and frame rate. The reconstruction is scored by adjacency accuracy: the fraction of consecutive true-neighbor pairs that are adjacent in the reported order must be >= 0.90 (direction may be forward or reversed; both accepted).
hardness_source: Three interacting facets: (1) a robust pairwise frame-similarity that survives compression noise and small lighting drift (not raw pixel diff); (2) chaining the pairwise graph into a single monotone path (a greedy nearest-neighbor walk fails at near-static stretches and repeated content, requiring a global path / MST-and-traverse or motion-direction consistency); (3) resolving the global direction ambiguity. Applied domain knowledge: optical-flow / feature-based frame similarity and sequence reconstruction. The held-out clips contain near-static runs and a brief repeated pan the example lacks, so a greedy pixel-diff chainer fails.
adversarial_cases: Held-out clips (never shown): one with a multi-frame near-static stretch (greedy chaining stalls / mis-links); one where the camera pans out and back over similar content (pixel-diff picks the wrong neighbor); one with heavy compression noise near the similarity threshold. Grading computes adjacency accuracy against the independently-known true order on clips the agent never saw.
trap: Greedy nearest-neighbor chaining on mean absolute pixel difference starting from an arbitrary frame — passes the smooth example, fails near-static/repeated-content held-out clips and the direction ambiguity.
why_hard: A first-pass pixel-diff greedy chainer passes the smooth example and fails held-out clips with near-static runs and repeated content; correctness needs a noise-robust similarity plus global path reconstruction that generalizes to unseen motion.
difficulty_summary: The agent must reconstruct the true temporal order of shuffled frames with >=0.90 adjacency accuracy on held-out fixed-camera clips using cv2/numpy, robust to near-static runs and repeated content.
graded_on: Adjacency accuracy (fraction of true consecutive pairs adjacent in the reported order) >= 0.90 on held-out clips, either direction accepted. Deterministic synthetic clips (fixed seed); tolerance-based, never byte-exact.
capability_name: Reconstruct temporal structure from unordered media

title: Count distinct objects crossing a line through occlusion
premise: In a fixed-camera clip, several similar objects move across the frame and cross a marked line; the count of DISTINCT objects that cross must be reported, and a naive per-frame blob count double-counts objects that pause on the line and merges objects that overlap while crossing.
spec: Write /app/counter.py (Python; cv2, numpy, toml only) that takes an MP4 path and writes /app/output.toml with field crossings = [integer], the number of distinct objects whose centroid crosses the horizontal line y = LINE_Y (a stated constant) from top to bottom over the clip. An example clip /app/example.mp4 with its known count is provided. Test clips share resolution/frame rate and LINE_Y. Scored: reported count within +/-0 for clips with <=5 objects and within +/-1 for busier clips (the exact inclusive tolerance per clip is stated to the grader).
hardness_source: Three interacting facets: (1) foreground segmentation robust to shadow and lighting so one object is one blob; (2) cross-frame data association (tracking) so an object that pauses on the line or is briefly occluded keeps ONE identity and is counted once; (3) directional crossing logic on the tracked centroid (top-to-bottom only), not per-frame line contact. Applied domain knowledge: background subtraction, centroid tracking / IoU association, occlusion handling. Held-out clips have two objects overlapping while crossing and one object pausing on the line — a per-frame counter double-counts or merges them.
adversarial_cases: Held-out clips (never shown): two similar objects overlap exactly while both crossing (naive blob count merges to one); an object stops on the line for several frames then continues (per-frame contact counts it many times); an object crosses partway, retreats, then crosses (must count once, in the correct direction). Grading compares to the independently-known distinct-crossing count within the stated per-clip tolerance.
trap: Counting frames where any foreground blob touches the line, or counting blobs per frame and summing — passes the clean example, fails occlusion/pause/retreat held-out clips.
why_hard: A per-frame blob-count solution passes the simple example and fails held-out clips with occlusion, pausing, and retreat; correctness needs identity-preserving tracking plus directional crossing logic that generalizes.
difficulty_summary: The agent must count distinct top-to-bottom line crossings within a stated tolerance on held-out clips using cv2/numpy, maintaining object identity through occlusion, pauses, and retreats.
graded_on: Reported crossing count within the stated per-clip inclusive tolerance on held-out clips. Deterministic synthetic clips (fixed seed); tolerance-based, never byte-exact.
capability_name: Track identity across frames under occlusion

title: Locate inserted duplicate and freeze frames in a stream
premise: A clip has had duplicate frames and short freeze runs inserted (a common transcoding/dropped-frame artifact); the exact set of inserted-duplicate frame indices must be reported, and a naive exact-equality check misses near-duplicates introduced by re-encoding.
spec: Write /app/dedup.py (Python; cv2, numpy, toml only) that takes an MP4 path and writes /app/output.toml with field duplicate_frames = [sorted list of 0-based indices that are duplicates of their immediately preceding kept frame]. An example clip /app/example.mp4 with its known duplicate set is provided. Test clips share resolution/frame rate. Scored by set F1 against the true duplicate set: F1 >= 0.90 required.
hardness_source: Three interacting facets: (1) distinguishing an inserted (near-)duplicate from genuine low-motion content — exact equality misses re-encoded duplicates, and a loose threshold flags slow real motion as duplicate; (2) handling multi-frame freeze RUNS so every inserted frame in the run is reported, not just the first; (3) anchoring indices to the ORIGINAL stream numbering as duplicates accumulate. Applied domain knowledge: perceptual frame similarity (SSIM / normalized correlation) with a principled threshold, run detection. Held-out clips contain a genuinely slow pan (must NOT be flagged) and a long freeze run the example lacks.
adversarial_cases: Held-out clips (never shown): a slow, smooth pan that a loose duplicate threshold false-flags; a 6-frame freeze run (must report all 6, not 1); re-encoded duplicates that are not byte-identical (exact-equality misses them). Grading computes set F1 vs the independently-known inserted-duplicate indices.
trap: Flagging frames where the exact pixel array equals the previous frame — misses re-encoded near-duplicates; or thresholding mean diff loosely — false-flags the slow pan.
why_hard: An exact-equality or loose-threshold detector passes the example and fails held-out clips with re-encoded duplicates, freeze runs, and slow real motion; correctness needs a calibrated perceptual-similarity criterion plus run handling that generalizes.
difficulty_summary: The agent must report the inserted-duplicate/freeze frame indices with set F1 >= 0.90 on held-out clips using cv2/numpy, separating re-encoded duplicates from slow genuine motion.
graded_on: Set F1 of reported duplicate indices vs the true inserted set >= 0.90 on held-out clips. Deterministic synthetic clips (fixed seed); tolerance-based, never byte-exact.

title: Estimate global camera motion despite foreground movement
premise: A clip is filmed by a panning/zooming camera while foreground objects move independently; the per-frame global camera motion (the background's dominant transform) must be estimated as a trajectory, and a naive average optical flow is corrupted by the moving foreground.
spec: Write /app/motion.py (Python; cv2, numpy, toml only) that takes an MP4 path and writes /app/output.toml with field dx = [list of per-frame horizontal camera translations in pixels] and dy = [list of per-frame vertical translations], one entry per frame transition (N-1 entries for N frames). An example clip /app/example.mp4 with its known camera trajectory is provided. Test clips share resolution/frame rate. Scored by mean absolute error against the true trajectory: MAE over all transitions <= 1.5 pixels on each axis.
hardness_source: Three interacting facets: (1) feature detection/matching between consecutive frames; (2) ROBUST model estimation that rejects the foreground object's motion as outliers (a plain average or dense-flow mean is dragged by the foreground — RANSAC / dominant-motion estimation is required); (3) accumulating per-frame estimates consistently without drift blowing past the MAE budget. Applied domain knowledge: feature matching, RANSAC/robust global-motion estimation, outlier rejection. Held-out clips have a large fast foreground object and a low-texture background region the example lacks.
adversarial_cases: Held-out clips (never shown): a large foreground object covering a third of the frame moving opposite the camera (mean flow points the wrong way); a low-texture background stretch (few reliable features); a fast pan near the per-frame displacement the naive method under-estimates. Grading computes per-axis MAE vs the independently-known camera trajectory.
trap: Averaging dense optical flow (or all feature displacements) to estimate camera motion — the moving foreground biases the average, failing every held-out clip with a large/fast foreground.
why_hard: A mean-optical-flow estimator passes the foreground-free example and fails held-out clips where foreground motion dominates the average; correctness needs robust outlier-rejecting global-motion estimation that generalizes.
difficulty_summary: The agent must estimate the per-frame global camera translation with per-axis MAE <= 1.5 px on held-out clips using cv2/numpy, rejecting independently-moving foreground as outliers.
graded_on: Per-axis mean absolute error of the reported dx/dy trajectory vs the true camera motion <= 1.5 px on held-out clips. Deterministic synthetic clips (fixed seed); tolerance-based, never byte-exact.
capability_name: Recover global motion robust to outliers

title: Measure a periodic rate from subtle pixel oscillation
premise: A clip shows a scene with a subtle periodic change (a blinking indicator, a spinning marker, or an oscillating element) partly obscured by noise and an unrelated slow brightness drift; the period (in frames) of the true oscillation must be measured, and a naive peak-count on raw intensity is fooled by noise and the drift.
spec: Write /app/period.py (Python; cv2, numpy, scipy, toml only) that takes an MP4 path and writes /app/output.toml with field period_frames = [float], the dominant period of the scene's true oscillation in frames. An example clip /app/example.mp4 with its known period is provided. Test clips share resolution/frame rate. Scored: reported period within +/-5% of the true period (inclusive relative tolerance).
hardness_source: Three interacting facets: (1) extracting a clean 1-D signal from the frames without being told the oscillating region's location (must find the region of maximal periodic energy, not average the whole frame); (2) removing the low-frequency brightness drift (detrend / high-pass) so it doesn't dominate; (3) robust frequency estimation (FFT / autocorrelation with peak interpolation) to get sub-frame period accuracy under noise. Applied domain knowledge: signal extraction from video, detrending, spectral estimation. Held-out clips add a stronger brightness drift and a smaller oscillating region than the example.
adversarial_cases: Held-out clips (never shown): a strong slow brightness ramp that a whole-frame-average peak counter locks onto instead of the oscillation; a small oscillating region (whole-frame averaging washes it out); additive noise near the oscillation amplitude requiring spectral rather than time-domain estimation. Grading compares the reported period to the independently-known period within +/-5%.
trap: Averaging whole-frame intensity and counting peaks over time — the brightness drift and noise dominate, and a small oscillating region is washed out, failing every held-out clip.
why_hard: A whole-frame peak-count solution passes the clean example and fails held-out clips with drift, a small region, and noise; correctness needs region-selective signal extraction, detrending, and spectral estimation that generalize.
difficulty_summary: The agent must measure the dominant oscillation period within +/-5% on held-out clips using cv2/numpy/scipy, isolating the periodic region and rejecting brightness drift and noise.
graded_on: Reported period_frames within +/-5% relative tolerance of the true period on held-out clips. Deterministic synthetic clips (fixed seed); tolerance-based, never byte-exact.
capability_name: Extract a periodic signal from noisy video
